parameters.query:
INSERT INTO management_results (
  instructor_id, term_id, subject_id, total_responses,
  m1_total, m2_total, m3_total, m4_total, m5_total,
  m6_total, m7_total, m8_total, m9_total, m10_total, grand_total,
  m1_mean, m2_mean, m3_mean, m4_mean, m5_mean,
  m6_mean, m7_mean, m8_mean, m9_mean, m10_mean,
  overall_management_mean, average_per_response_management
) VALUES (
  $1::uuid, $2::uuid, $3::uuid, $4::numeric,
  $5::numeric, $6::numeric, $7::numeric, $8::numeric, $9::numeric,
  $10::numeric, $11::numeric, $12::numeric, $13::numeric, $14::numeric, $15::numeric,
  $16::numeric, $17::numeric, $18::numeric, $19::numeric, $20::numeric,
  $21::numeric, $22::numeric, $23::numeric, $24::numeric, $25::numeric,
  $26::numeric, $27::numeric
)
ON CONFLICT (instructor_id, term_id, subject_id) DO UPDATE SET
  total_responses = EXCLUDED.total_responses,
  m1_total = EXCLUDED.m1_total, m2_total = EXCLUDED.m2_total,
  m3_total = EXCLUDED.m3_total, m4_total = EXCLUDED.m4_total,
  m5_total = EXCLUDED.m5_total, m6_total = EXCLUDED.m6_total,
  m7_total = EXCLUDED.m7_total, m8_total = EXCLUDED.m8_total,
  m9_total = EXCLUDED.m9_total, m10_total = EXCLUDED.m10_total,
  grand_total = EXCLUDED.grand_total,
  m1_mean = EXCLUDED.m1_mean, m2_mean = EXCLUDED.m2_mean,
  m3_mean = EXCLUDED.m3_mean, m4_mean = EXCLUDED.m4_mean,
  m5_mean = EXCLUDED.m5_mean, m6_mean = EXCLUDED.m6_mean,
  m7_mean = EXCLUDED.m7_mean, m8_mean = EXCLUDED.m8_mean,
  m9_mean = EXCLUDED.m9_mean, m10_mean = EXCLUDED.m10_mean,
  overall_management_mean = EXCLUDED.overall_management_mean,
  average_per_response_management = EXCLUDED.average_per_response_management

INSERT INTO performance_results (
  instructor_id, term_id, subject_id, total_responses,
  p1_total, p2_total, p3_total, p4_total, p5_total,
  p6_total, p7_total, p8_total, p9_total, p10_total, grand_total,
  p1_mean, p2_mean, p3_mean, p4_mean, p5_mean,
  p6_mean, p7_mean, p8_mean, p9_mean, p10_mean,
  overall_performance_mean, average_per_response_performance
) VALUES (
  $1::uuid, $2::uuid, $3::uuid, $4::numeric,
  $5::numeric, $6::numeric, $7::numeric, $8::numeric, $9::numeric,
  $10::numeric, $11::numeric, $12::numeric, $13::numeric, $14::numeric, $15::numeric,
  $16::numeric, $17::numeric, $18::numeric, $19::numeric, $20::numeric,
  $21::numeric, $22::numeric, $23::numeric, $24::numeric, $25::numeric,
  $26::numeric, $27::numeric
)
ON CONFLICT (instructor_id, term_id, subject_id) DO UPDATE SET
  total_responses = EXCLUDED.total_responses,
  p1_total = EXCLUDED.p1_total, p2_total = EXCLUDED.p2_total,
  p3_total = EXCLUDED.p3_total, p4_total = EXCLUDED.p4_total,
  p5_total = EXCLUDED.p5_total, p6_total = EXCLUDED.p6_total,
  p7_total = EXCLUDED.p7_total, p8_total = EXCLUDED.p8_total,
  p9_total = EXCLUDED.p9_total, p10_total = EXCLUDED.p10_total,
  grand_total = EXCLUDED.grand_total,
  p1_mean = EXCLUDED.p1_mean, p2_mean = EXCLUDED.p2_mean,
  p3_mean = EXCLUDED.p3_mean, p4_mean = EXCLUDED.p4_mean,
  p5_mean = EXCLUDED.p5_mean, p6_mean = EXCLUDED.p6_mean,
  p7_mean = EXCLUDED.p7_mean, p8_mean = EXCLUDED.p8_mean,
  p9_mean = EXCLUDED.p9_mean, p10_mean = EXCLUDED.p10_mean,
  overall_performance_mean = EXCLUDED.overall_performance_mean,
  average_per_response_performance = EXCLUDED.average_per_response_performance

WITH mgmt_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    COALESCE(SUM(total_responses), 0) AS m_total_resp,
    COALESCE(SUM(grand_total), 0) AS m_total,
    COALESCE(SUM(grand_total)::numeric / NULLIF(SUM(total_responses) * 10, 0), 0) AS m_avg
  FROM public.management_results
  WHERE instructor_id = $1::uuid AND term_id = $2::uuid
),
perf_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    COALESCE(SUM(total_responses), 0) AS p_total_resp,
    COALESCE(SUM(grand_total), 0) AS p_total,
    COALESCE(SUM(grand_total)::numeric / NULLIF(SUM(total_responses) * 10, 0), 0) AS p_avg
  FROM public.performance_results
  WHERE instructor_id = $1::uuid AND term_id = $2::uuid
)
INSERT INTO public.overall_total_survey (
  instructor_id, term_id, total_responses, management_total, performance_total, combined_total, management_mean, performance_mean, combined_score_mean
)
SELECT 
  $1::uuid, $2::uuid, 
  m.m_total_resp, 
  m.m_total, p.p_total, 
  (m.m_total + p.p_total), 
  m.m_avg, 
  p.p_avg, 
  (m.m_total + p.p_total)::numeric / NULLIF((m.m_total_resp * 10) + (p.p_total_resp * 10), 0)
FROM mgmt_stats m, perf_stats p
ON CONFLICT (instructor_id, term_id) 
DO UPDATE SET 
  total_responses = EXCLUDED.total_responses,
  management_total = EXCLUDED.management_total,
  performance_total = EXCLUDED.performance_total,
  combined_total = EXCLUDED.combined_total,
  management_mean = EXCLUDED.management_mean,
  performance_mean = EXCLUDED.performance_mean,
  combined_score_mean = EXCLUDED.combined_score_mean
RETURNING instructor_id, term_id, combined_score_mean;

SELECT 
  s.id AS subject_id, 
  s.subject_code, 
  s.subject_name,
  s.department_id,

JOIN public.instructor_subjects ins

  AND ins.instructor_id = $1
  AND ins.term_id = (
    SELECT current_term_id 
    FROM public.system_settings

  )
ORDER BY similarity(
  COALESCE(s.subject_code, '') || ' ' || COALESCE(s.subject_name, ''), 
  $2
) DESC 
LIMIT 1;

SELECT (
    SELECT id
    FROM public.user_info
    WHERE $1 ILIKE '%' || first_name || '%' 
      AND $1 ILIKE '%' || last_name || '%'
    LIMIT 1
) AS "instructor_ID";

INSERT INTO public.subjects (subject_code, subject_name, department_id)
VALUES (
    $1, 
    $2, 
    (SELECT id FROM public.department_name WHERE d_name = $3 LIMIT 1)
)
ON CONFLICT (subject_code) 
DO UPDATE SET 
    subject_name = EXCLUDED.subject_name,
    department_id = COALESCE(EXCLUDED.department_id, subjects.department_id)
RETURNING id AS subject_id, department_id;

parameters.query:
WITH matched_subject AS (
  SELECT s.id AS subject_id, s.subject_code, s.subject_name, s.department_id
  FROM public.subjects s
  ORDER BY similarity(COALESCE(s.subject_code, '') || ' ' || COALESCE(s.subject_name, ''), $2) DESC
  LIMIT 1
),
assign_instructor AS (
  INSERT INTO public.instructor_subjects (subject_id, instructor_id, term_id)
  SELECT 
    ms.subject_id, 
    $1::uuid, 
    (SELECT current_term_id FROM public.system_settings LIMIT 1)
  FROM matched_subject ms
  WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM public.instructor_subjects ins 
    WHERE ins.subject_id = ms.subject_id 
      AND ins.instructor_id = $1::uuid 
      AND ins.term_id = (SELECT current_term_id FROM public.system_settings LIMIT 1)
  )
  AND (SELECT current_term_id FROM public.system_settings LIMIT 1) IS NOT NULL
  RETURNING id
)
SELECT 
  ms.subject_id, 
  ms.subject_code, 
  ms.subject_name, 
  ms.department_id,
  $1 AS instructor_id,
  CASE WHEN ai.id IS NOT NULL THEN true ELSE false END AS was_just_assigned
FROM matched_subject ms
LEFT JOIN assign_instructor ai ON true;

parameters.text:
=You are the analysis engine for a university instructor evaluation system.

You are analyzing NEW student remarks for ONE instructor and ONE academic term.

Your job is to:

1. Analyze the new remarks.
2. Update the existing instructor analysis using historical context.
3. Identify keyword/theme support from ONLY the new remarks.
4. Classify the tone of EVERY new remark.
5. Determine the cumulative overall tone.

============================================================
CRITICAL DATA RULE
============================================================

There are TWO different datasets:

HISTORICAL DATA:
- previous_analysis
- previous_wordcloud
- previous_remarks

NEW DATA:
- feedback

Historical data has already been processed.

NEVER count historical remarks as new remarks.

NEVER include historical wordcloud counts in keyword new_count.

NEVER return historical remarks in remark_tones.

The database will add keyword new_count to the existing wordcloud count.

============================================================
NEW REMARKS
============================================================

Each feedback item has:

- index
- remark
- subject_id
- source_response_id

The index is supplied by the system.

Never change it.

Every feedback item MUST produce exactly one remark_tones result.

If there are 8 feedback items, return exactly 8 remark_tones objects.

============================================================
KEYWORDS
============================================================

Analyze ONLY the NEW feedback when generating keyword counts.

For every keyword:

new_count =
the number of UNIQUE NEW feedback indexes that support the
keyword.

Example:

Feedback 1:
"Maayo kaayo mo explain."

Feedback 2:
"Klaro kaayo ang discussion."

Feedback 3:
"Maayo ang explanation."

All three support:

Teaching clarity

Therefore:

{
  "word": "Teaching clarity",
  "new_count": 3
}

IMPORTANT:

Do NOT count word occurrences.

Do NOT count repeated words.

Do NOT count repeated phrases.

Do NOT count historical remarks.

Do NOT use previous_wordcloud counts in new_count.

Each feedback index can contribute maximum 1 count
to the same keyword.

One feedback item may support multiple different keywords.

Maximum 10 keywords.

Only return keywords supported by the NEW feedback.

============================================================
KEYWORD FORMAT
============================================================

Each keyword must contain 1-3 words.

Prefer concise English theme names.

Examples:

Teaching clarity
Classroom management
More examples
Pacing
Student engagement

============================================================
INSTRUCTOR INTERPRETATION
============================================================

Use:

- previous_analysis
- previous_wordcloud
- previous_remarks
- feedback

The result should represent the instructor's overall evaluation based on combined evidence.

Do NOT mention:

- previous surveys
- historical data
- new batch
- updated analysis
- AI
- wordcloud

Write naturally as an instructor evaluation summary.

Do not invent information.

============================================================
POSITIVES
============================================================

Identify positive themes supported by the combined evidence.

Keep valid historical strengths when the evidence still supports them.

Add new strengths only when supported by feedback.

Do not invent strengths.

============================================================
IMPROVEMENTS
============================================================

Identify improvement areas supported by the combined evidence.

Keep valid historical improvement areas when still relevant.

Add new improvement areas only when supported by feedback.

Do not invent problems.

============================================================
SUGGESTION
============================================================

Give ONE concise, constructive, actionable recommendation.

The recommendation must directly correspond to an improvement area supported by the feedback.

Do not introduce unrelated recommendations.

============================================================
REMARK TONE
============================================================

Classify EVERY NEW feedback item.

Allowed values:

Positive
Critical
Neutral

Positive:
Praise, satisfaction, appreciation, or positive experience.

Critical:
Complaint, concern, dissatisfaction, criticism, or request for improvement.

Neutral:
Factual, unclear, informational, or neither clearly positive nor critical.

Understand:

- English
- Tagalog
- Bisaya/Cebuano
- mixed English/Tagalog
- mixed English/Bisaya
- mixed Tagalog/Bisaya

Examples:

"Maayo kaayo mo explain si ma'am."
Positive

"Klaro kaayo ang discussion."
Positive

"Dugangi pa unta ang examples."
Critical

"Mas maayo unta kung hinay-hinayan ang discussion."
Critical

"Okay ra man."
Neutral

============================================================
OVERALL TONE
============================================================

Determine overall_tone from the COMBINED historical and new student remarks.

Each student remark has equal weight.

Count each remark once.

Positive = largest count
Critical = largest count
Neutral = largest count

If there is a tie, return Neutral.

Allowed values:

Positive
Critical
Neutral

Do not determine tone from:

- remark length
- number of words
- number of sentences
- emotional intensity

============================================================
OUTPUT
============================================================

Return ONLY valid JSON.

No markdown.

No code fences.

Use exactly:

{
  "keywords": [
    {
      "word": "Teaching clarity",
      "new_count": 2
    }
  ],
  "evaluation": {
    "interpretation": "",
    "positives": "",
    "improvements": "",
    "suggestion": ""
  },
  "overall_tone": "Positive",
  "remark_tones": [
    {
      "index": 1,
      "tone": "Positive"
    }
  ]
}

============================================================
FINAL CHECK
============================================================

Before returning:

- valid JSON
- maximum 10 keywords
- keyword is 1-3 words
- every keyword supported by NEW feedback
- new_count is integer >= 1
- new_count counts unique NEW indexes
- no historical counts included
- no historical remarks included in remark_tones
- evaluation contains exactly four fields
- evaluation fields are strings
- overall_tone is Positive, Critical, or Neutral
- exactly one remark_tones object per NEW feedback item
- every supplied NEW index appears exactly once
- no invented information
- no invented counts
- no invented keywords
- no invented recommendations

============================================================
HISTORICAL ANALYSIS
============================================================

{{ JSON.stringify($json.previous_analysis) }}

============================================================
HISTORICAL WORDCLOUD
============================================================

{{ JSON.stringify($json.previous_wordcloud) }}

============================================================
HISTORICAL REMARKS
============================================================

{{ JSON.stringify($json.previous_remarks) }}

============================================================
NEW FEEDBACK
============================================================

{{ JSON.stringify($json.feedback) }}

parameters.query:
SELECT

    $1::uuid AS instructor_id,

    $2::uuid AS term_id,

    COALESCE(
        (
            SELECT jsonb_build_object(

                'ai_suggestion',
                ai.ai_suggestion,

                'student_interpretation',
                ai.student_interpretation,

                'positive_themes',
                ai.positive_themes,

                'improvement_insights',
                ai.improvement_insights,

                'overall_tone',
                ai.overall_tone

            )

            FROM public.instructor_ai_suggestions ai

            WHERE ai.instructor_id = $1::uuid

              AND ai.term_id = $2::uuid

            LIMIT 1
        ),

        '{}'::jsonb
    ) AS previous_analysis,


    COALESCE(
        (
            SELECT jsonb_agg(
                jsonb_build_object(

                    'word',
                    wc.word,

                    'count',
                    wc.count

                )

                ORDER BY
                    wc.count DESC,
                    wc.word ASC

            )

            FROM public.instructor_wordcloud wc

            WHERE wc.instructor_id = $1::uuid

              AND wc.term_id = $2::uuid
        ),

        '[]'::jsonb

    ) AS previous_wordcloud,


    COALESCE(
        (
            SELECT jsonb_agg(
                jsonb_build_object(

                    'subject_id',
                    x.subject_id,

                    'remark',
                    x.remark,

                    'tone',
                    x.tone,

                    'created_at',
                    x.created_at

                )

                ORDER BY
                    x.created_at DESC

            )

            FROM (

                SELECT
                    sr.subject_id,
                    sr.remark,
                    sr.tone,
                    sr.created_at

                FROM public.student_remarks sr

                WHERE sr.instructor_id = $1::uuid

                  AND sr.term_id = $2::uuid

                ORDER BY
                    sr.created_at DESC

                LIMIT 100

            ) x

        ),

        '[]'::jsonb

    ) AS previous_remarks;

parameters.text:
=You are an AI analysis system for a university instructor evaluation system.

You are processing ONE NEW student evaluation.

Your task is to UPDATE the existing instructor analysis using the new student feedback.

You have three sources of information:

1. EXISTING AI ANALYSIS
2. EXISTING WORDCLOUD
3. NEW STUDENT FEEDBACK

The existing AI analysis represents all previous student feedback that has already been processed.

The new student feedback is ADDITIONAL evidence.

==================================================
EXISTING AI ANALYSIS
==================================================

{{ JSON.stringify($json.existing_ai) }}

==================================================
EXISTING WORDCLOUD
==================================================

{{ JSON.stringify($json.existing_wordcloud) }}

==================================================
NEW STUDENT FEEDBACK
==================================================

{{ $json.new_student_remark }}

==================================================
IMPORTANT ANALYSIS RULES
==================================================

1. Do not ignore the existing AI analysis.

2. Do not completely replace the existing analysis with information from only the new student.

3. Treat the existing AI analysis as the previous accumulated analysis.

4. Treat the new student feedback as additional evidence.

5. Update the analysis only when the new feedback provides relevant information.

6. Do not invent information.

7. Do not remove valid information from the existing analysis unless the new evidence clearly contradicts it.

8. The updated analysis should represent BOTH:
   - previous student feedback
   - the new student feedback

9. The new student feedback must influence the result when it contains meaningful information.

10. If the new feedback is positive, incorporate its positive information.

11. If the new feedback identifies an improvement area, incorporate that improvement area.

12. The overall tone should represent the NEW student feedback, not the entire historical dataset.

==================================================
STUDENT INTERPRETATION
==================================================

Write a short interpretation of what the NEW student is communicating.

Do not invent information.

==================================================
POSITIVE THEMES
==================================================

Update the positive themes based on the existing analysis and the new feedback.

Keep existing valid themes.

Add a new theme only when the new feedback supports it.

Avoid duplicates and different phrases describing the same concept.

==================================================
IMPROVEMENT INSIGHTS
==================================================

Update the improvement insights based on the existing analysis and the new feedback.

Keep existing valid insights.

Add a new insight only when the new feedback supports it.

Avoid duplicates and different phrases describing the same concept.

==================================================
AI SUGGESTION
==================================================

Create an UPDATED instructor suggestion.

The suggestion must consider both the existing analysis and the new student feedback.

Do not simply copy the existing suggestion.

If the new feedback provides a new improvement area, incorporate it naturally.

If the new feedback only reinforces an existing issue, strengthen the existing recommendation rather than creating a duplicate recommendation.

The suggestion should be concise, professional, constructive, and suitable for an instructor evaluation report.

==================================================
OVERALL TONE
==================================================

Determine the tone of the NEW student feedback.

The value MUST be exactly one of:

Positive
Critical
Neutral

Positive:
The student mainly expresses praise, satisfaction, appreciation, or a positive experience.

Critical:
The student mainly expresses a complaint, concern, dissatisfaction, criticism, or request for improvement.

Neutral:
The feedback is factual, unclear, or does not clearly express positive or critical sentiment.

Examples:

"Very good instructor."
→ Positive

"Maayo kaayo siya mo explain."
→ Positive

"Please give more examples."
→ Critical

"Dugangi unta ang examples."
→ Critical

"His class is every Monday."
→ Neutral

==================================================
WORDCLOUD
==================================================

Extract meaningful keywords from the NEW student feedback.

Maximum 5 keywords.

You must return AT LEAST 1 keyword, even if the feedback is vague, short, or emotional.

If the feedback does not contain a specific concrete theme, extract the closest general theme it relates to, such as:
"Teaching quality"
"Attitude"
"Fairness"
"Communication"
"Professionalism"
"Classroom management"

Only return zero keywords if the feedback text is completely empty or unreadable.

Each keyword must contain 1–3 words.

Normalize Tagalog and Bisaya/Cebuano concepts into concise English themes when appropriate.

Remove filler words.

Remove meaningless emotional words on their own (e.g. do not return just "Bad" or "Good"), but you may still capture the underlying theme those words point to (e.g. "Teaching quality").

Do not use vague keywords such as:
"Good"
"Nice"
"Okay"
"Instructor"
unless the word represents a meaningful theme.

==================================================
WORDCLOUD DUPLICATE RULE
==================================================

The EXISTING WORDCLOUD contains previously stored concepts.

If the new feedback represents the SAME concept as an existing word, use the EXISTING WORD exactly.

Example:

Existing word:
"Examples"

New feedback:
"Please provide more examples."

Correct:
"Examples"

Incorrect:
"More examples"

Another example:

Existing word:
"Teaching clarity"

New feedback:
"Maayo kaayo mo explain."

Correct:
"Teaching clarity"

Do NOT create duplicate concepts such as:
"Clear explanation"
"Good explanation"
"Explanation clarity"
if "Teaching clarity" already exists.

Every returned keyword must have:
"count": 1

The database will add this count to the existing wordcloud.

==================================================
OUTPUT FORMAT
==================================================

Return ONLY valid JSON.

Do NOT return:
- Markdown
- ```json
- Explanation
- Comments
- Extra text

Use exactly this structure:

{
  "ai_suggestion": "Updated instructor suggestion...",
  "student_interpretation": "Short interpretation of the new student feedback.",
  "positive_themes": [
    "Teaching clarity"
  ],
  "improvement_insights": [
    "Examples"
  ],
  "overall_tone": "Critical",
  "keywords": [
    {
      "word": "Teaching clarity",
      "count": 1
    },
    {
      "word": "Examples",
      "count": 1
    }
  ]
}

IMPORTANT:
- overall_tone MUST be exactly Positive, Critical, or Neutral.
- keywords MUST be an array.
- keywords MUST contain at least 1 item.
- Maximum 5 keywords.
- Every keyword count MUST be 1.
- Do not invent keywords unrelated to the feedback.
- Do not invent information.
- Return valid JSON only.
